source.title: [Bounty] Answer the 2 linked question(s)
source.body:
# [Bounty] Answer the 2 linked question(s) ## Context These intakes ask about something no lesson covers. Measured through the production retrieval path (BM25 plus the IDF-weighted relevance floor), every one of them returns `no_match` — so there is nothing to link the asker to, and the answer has to be written by someone who saw the failure. - #2476 — [Question] How should native macOS UI automation recover from noWindowsAvailable (-10005) w - #3607 — [Question] Native UI automation returned 'The user changed app. Re-query the latest state w _Shared vocabulary that grouped them: `accessibility`, `actions`, `automation`, `native`._ ## Deliverable **An answer, posted as a comment on each question issue above.** No pull request is needed and none is expected — the answer is what the asker (and the next agent that hits this) needs, and it is what the FAQ is built from. `sync-question-answers.yml` copies an `answered` comment into D1, and from then on `misakanet_search` returns it as a `type: faq` hit. The answer has to be *observed*, not generated. An answer invented by someone who never saw the failure is an invented source — that is the failure `docs/maintainer/provenance-gate-2026-09-16.md` exists to prevent. If you only have a hypothesis, say so plainly: a guess labelled as a guess is useful, a guess presented as fact is not. ## How your answer reaches readers 1. Post it on **each** linked question issue as a comment — not only here. The sync reads the question's own thread. 2. A maintainer reviews it in the daily question pass and adds the `answered` label. 3. `sync-question-answers.yml` copies the labelled comment into the FAQ (D1) within a day. ## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (AC) **0. REPRODUCIBLE EVIDENCE — the condition most submissions fail** - [ ] Paste the command you ran and the output you got. Not a description of what you did — the command and its output. If you name an endpoint it must be `misakanet.org`. - [ ] Say what you observed yourself versus what you read somewhere. **1. The answer is complete** - [ ] It states the root cause, the fix (with the exact command or setting), and how to check it worked — the last one is a command plus the result that means success, not "it should work". - [ ] It names the version / environment it was observed on. "Works on my machine" without that line is unfalsifiable. **2. It is posted where the question lives** - [ ] A comment on **every** linked question issue above. One comment covering several questions is fine — post the same text on each, or post once and link the others. **3. Claiming** - [ ] Comment `/try` (or `/claim`) here so others know you are on it; the claim rules are in `JOIN.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. ## What the reward is, stated plainly **This is a `zero-bounty` task: $0.** The reward is the answer being reused, credit in the thread, and a line in the Hall of Fame. A real bounty exists only when someone funds it by commenting `/reward ` on this issue — the money is held and paid by Opire, not by this repository. ## Optional: also land it as a lesson Never required for this task. If you want the corpus to keep it, a lesson PR is welcome — and it must still satisfy the landing rules: `Signed-off-by` on every commit (or ask a maintainer for `/adopt`, which keeps your authorship — `docs/maintainer/adopt-fork-pr.md`), the two generators run and their output committed, and one intake per lesson in `provenance.issue` (the rest in `provenance.related`, per #3361). Say here first if you plan to open one. ## Closes An answer closes this task once a maintainer labels it `answered`; the questions above close the same way. If a lesson lands instead, `Fixes #N` closes them through the receipt rule. If you cannot finish it, comment here and it goes back to the pool. Opened automatically by `scripts/question_autopilot.py` from measured coverage of the open questions. The grouping is a suggestion: if these are not really one question, say so and this task will be split.
This repo is using Opire - what does it mean? 👇
💵 Everyone can add rewards for this issue commenting /reward 100 (replace 100 with the amount).
🕵️‍♂️ If someone starts working on this issue to earn the rewards, they can comment /try to let everyone know!
🙌 And when they open the PR, they can comment /claim #4133 either in the PR description or in a PR's comment.

🪙 Also, everyone can tip any user commenting /tip 20 @github-actions[bot] (replace 20 with the amount, and @github-actions[bot] with the user to tip).

📖 If you want to learn more, check out our documentation.
